Four snapshots of Syria's war, from 2015 to 2021, show control of the country changing hands again and again. The map stops in 2021. The story didn't.

a thread 🧵🗺️
1/ The war began with protests on 15 March 2011. In 2014 the Islamic State seized large areas of eastern Syria, which is the black zone on the 2015 and 2016 panels.
2/ The green area is the Kurdish-led Autonomous Administration, which gained de facto autonomy in 2012. Its SDF force received US-led coalition support against the Islamic State.
3/ Turkey, in dark blue on the later panels, invaded northern Syria in 2016 and launched another offensive after the US withdrawal in October 2019.
4/ By 2021 the red government zone covers most of the country, and the rebel pocket in Idlib is tiny. A ceasefire there held from 2020 until November 2024.
5/ Then it changed fast. On 27 November 2024, an opposition offensive led by Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham began. On 8 December Assad fled to Moscow, and Ahmed al-Sharaa became de facto leader.
6/ The human cost is huge. The UN Commission of Inquiry counted more than 580,000 people killed from 2011 to May 2021, and about 6.7 million were internally displaced by March 2021.
7/ What would you want an updated map of Syria to show? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
